newsitem.title: UK: New British pension compensation scheme launched.
newsitem.headline: New British pension compensation scheme launched.

text.p: A new independent financial safety net for Britain's 11 million members of occupational pension schemes was launched on Monday.
The Pensions Compensation Scheme covers fund losses caused by dishonesty which the employer cannot make good because of insolvency.

The scheme follows a recommendation by the Goode committee set up by the government in the wake of the Maxwell pensions scandal in 1991 that the various protective provisions of the 1995 Pensions Act be backed up by establishing an independent compensation scheme.
Speaking at its launch, Dr Julian Farrand, chairman of the Pensions Compensation Board, said that the scheme should be seen as "back-up" insurance for pension funds, not as an "all-risks" policy.
The maximum payable will be 90 percent of the loss or the amount needed to restore the scheme to 90 percent funding.
Comparable compensation schemes already exist, covering investment losses, criminal injuries and bank, building society or insurance company collapses.
